newsitem.title: UK: FTSE seen scaling new peaks next week, eyes RPI.
newsitem.headline: FTSE seen scaling new peaks next week, eyes RPI.

text.p: London's FTSE 100 share index is set to steam higher into record territory next week unless derailed by strong British inflation data or weak blue-chip profits, analysts said.

The FTSE advanced to new heights on Friday, breaking through the 4,300 barrier on benign U.S. employment figures. Analysts said the UK Producer Price Index (PPI) on Monday and Retail Price Index (RPI) on Thursday would set the tone for next week.
"We might well see new record levels next week," said Richard Jeffrey, head of research at Charterhouse Tilney.

"But we have a lot of inflation data next week which will be important, culminating with Thursday's retail price index," he said. "It might well be that if those numbers are higher than anticipated, the market could be shaken a little bit."

Analysts polled by Reuters expect a 5.7 percent annualised fall in Monday's PPI for input prices and a 1.6 percent rise in the PPI for output prices. The average forecast for Thusday's January RPI is a 2.7 percent annualised increase.
"Those figures will be closely watched, given the disagreements between the Chancellor and the Bank of England over the threat of inflation," one trader said.

Bank of England governor Eddie George has called for a half-point hike in interest rates but Chancellor Kenneth Clarke has resisted the pressure and analysts do not expect a rate rise ahead of the British election, which must be held by May 22.

Other British data next week includes average earnings for December and January unemployment, both due on Wednesday. U.S. January producer prices data on Friday is the main international release to watch, dealers said.
"The U.S. situation looks fairly sound, and the latest payrolls figures have given the market another boost," a dealer said. "But the Dow has been volatile and could be upset again."

Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International in London, believes the FTSE 100 could test the 4,400 to 4,450 level over the next few months as investors anticipate steady interest rates in both the U.S. and the UK.

"As long as the market's attention is on low interest rates, equities will rally from here," Shah said. "But the market could be in for a nasty shock next quarter if the strong dollar has an impact on earnings."
Currency factors will also remain important for British stocks. "Sterling's strength looks like persisting and that could have a negative effect of the FTSE," one dealer said.
Company results will have an important bearing next week as the reporting season begins in earnest, dealers said.
Six FTSE companies are due to report results. Tuesday sees full-year figures from British Petroleum Plc, Reuters Holdings Plc and Unilever Plc, along with third-quarter profits from British Airways.
Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc reports annual results on Thursday and Lloyds TSB Group Plc on Friday.
Dealers said some investors had been staying out of the market until the reporting season got underway and the level of corporate earnings could be gauged.
Some said earnings would be generally weaker than expected and could trip up the FTSE's bull run.
But Jeffrey said unremarkable results were largely expected and surprises were as likely to be positive as negative.
"What people are anticipating is downgrades so anything better than that is going to be good news," he said.
"People expect companies to be talking about the strength of sterling and so on. But there is hope for positive surprises," Jeffrey told Reuters.
